title: LLMs Simulate the Description of a Culture, Not the Culture: paper, code, data and pre-registration files
description:
Replication package for the paper LLMs Simulate the Description of a Culture, Not the Culture: An Attempt to Reproduce Henrich's Cross-Cultural Ultimatum Game Finding with LLM Agents.

The package contains the paper in English and Turkish (LaTeX sources and PDFs), all experiment code and prompts, the identity descriptions, the written hypothesis and analysis-plan files of every test with their dated amendments, the results of every run, the raw log of every API call (account identifier redacted), the analysis scripts, and a lab notebook that records each analysis step including withdrawn claims.

Three model families (Claude Haiku 4.5, Gemma-4-31b-it, GPT-OSS-120b) played the one-shot Ultimatum Game as responders described by WEIRD or small-scale identity cards. For the same identities, game and offers, the outcome changed with the wording of the identity description: a numeric fairness score on the card largely determined the rejection rate; without numbers, a gap opposite to Henrich's field data appeared, but only when the description contained value-laden phrases such as reciprocity, sharing and kin network; with a minimal or a factual description the gap between arms vanished. No description reproduced the human pattern.

The hypothesis files were written before each test's data were collected but were not uploaded to a public time-stamped registry.
